summary.headline: Digilogic H1 FY27 revenue rose 91% to INR34.96 crores and PAT rose 151% to INR4.76 crores, with management reiterating 25-30% FY27 top-line growth.
summary.overview: H1 FY27 revenue grew 91% to INR34.96 crores from INR18 crores, EBITDA rose 126% to INR7.81 crores, and PAT grew 151% to INR4.76 crores. Management said H2 is seasonally much stronger in defense, citing FY26 revenue of INR78 crores split as H1 INR19 crores and H2 INR59 crores. Order book of INR20 crores is to be billed by mid-February 2027, with a further INR54 crores in pipeline at various tender stages. Management also reiterated 25-30% top-line and 30-35% EBITDA/PAT growth guidance for FY27, though analysts noted that the EBITDA guidance was lowered from 45-50% and that H1 margin gains were partly driven by FD interest income.

financial_highlights.value: INR78 crores (H1 INR19 crores, H2 INR59 crores)

segments.name: Test, measurement and simulation systems (TMS)
segments.commentary: Core business, described as the heart of operations; 36 projects executed in H1 FY27 valued at around INR33.18 crores. Customers include PSUs and DRDO agencies. Management expects TMS to keep growing at 20-30% a year.

segments.name: Abhedya Systems (wholly owned subsidiary, R&D)
segments.commentary: New experts hired for R&D; commercial production expected in H2 FY29 if plans hold. Management did not disclose financials.

segments.name: Project Udaan (new facility, build-to-print and build-to-spec)
segments.commentary: Civil construction is ongoing, with first-floor roof concrete complete; completion targeted by March 2027 and operations by end-2027. Management expects certification around Q1 2028 and commercialisation in about two years, with contribution starting FY28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth guidance of 25-30%, which management said it expects to meet; CFO said the company expects to touch its guidance number.
EBITDA and PAT growth guidance of 30-35%. The CFO said the 40-45% figure in the earlier outlook included FD interest income, and core growth stays at 30-35%.
Management said the current margins are sustainable, with no guidance to expand or contract.
Order book of INR20 crores and pipeline of INR54 crores targeted for billing by mid-February 2027.
Project Udaan: civil construction completion by March 2027, internal testing by December 2027, inspection and certification in Q1 2028, and about three months to get the certificate.
High Precision GIMBAL System and custom single-board computer products expected to be marketable around mid-2027, adding an estimated INR3-4 crores a year initially, with break-even thereafter.
Ongoing internal SOP and technology upgrade expected to finish between December 2026 and March 2027.
capex_capacity: Project Udaan is a new facility whose civil construction is in progress. Management expects operations from end-2027 and certification around Q1 2028.
Abhedya Systems (wholly owned subsidiary) is expected to start commercial production in H2 FY29.
Management said the Udaan facility will cover both build-to-spec (in-house design) and build-to-print (production of designs supplied by clients), with build-to-print expected to contribute first.
Inventory rose in H1 because of work-in-progress and pre-ordered long-lead items for orders due by mid-February 2027. Management said this stock will be consumed by March.
demand_pricing: Management said the order book is INR20 crores and the pipeline INR54 crores, with about 60% of the pipeline being repeat orders. Total of around INR74 crores is described as converted from the INR110 crores tender pipeline cited in May 2026.
All INR22 crores of order spillover from the prior period was billed in H1 FY27, according to management.
Management said it could not share the split of the INR54 crores between technical evaluation, commercial negotiation and pending purchase orders. Government procurement timelines vary.
Competitive moat: management said customised boards, signal processing and software go through R&QA certification by government agencies, which it says takes 2-3 years to replicate.
Analysts asked for a segment split. The CFO said the H1 segment data was not readily available and would be shared later.
The company said it has no export sales; all revenue is domestic.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the EBITDA guidance reduced from 45-50% to 30-35%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said core growth is 30-35%; the earlier 40-45% figure included FD interest income. He said the core growth guidance is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Was the INR22 crore spillover from the last call completed in H1?
qa_highlights.answer: MD said all spillover orders were billed in H1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the H1 margin improvement driven by, including software value-add?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the margin gains are driven by FD interest income, with fixed costs steady. He said the gains are across the board and not from software or revenue mix, and that segment-level analysis had not been done for the limited review.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 revenue reach the guidance (INR100 crore-plus implied H2 of about INR65 crores)?
qa_highlights.answer: MD said the 25-30% target is supported by the INR20 crore order book and the INR54 crore pipeline; he called anything above it a bonus.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline and role of the new Udaan facility, and what does it add to revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: MD said Udaan will start contributing in FY28 and that TMS will continue to grow alongside it. Management declined to quantify the Udaan revenue contribution.

qa_highlights.question: How do defense program delays (QRSAM, P-75I, NGC) affect the order intake?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said Digilogic is part of about 10 programmes, of which 3-4 have moved into production, so TMS has not been impacted by the delays.

risks_watch: Order book is INR20 crores, lower than earlier disclosures; the INR54 crore pipeline is not yet awarded and management would not give a split by stage.
H2 must deliver about INR65 crores of revenue to reach FY27 guidance (implied by analyst math), which is heavily dependent on billing by mid-February 2027.
Project Udaan has schedule risk: civil completion by March 2027, certification in Q1 2028, then about 3 months for certification. Management did not quantify Udaan revenue.
Margin gains partly came from FD interest income; the company has not yet split segment profitability.
Government procurement delays; sales cycles depend on tender stages and purchase orders.
Segment revenue split and export data were requested but not provided on the call; the company said it would follow up.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the 25-30% top-line and 30-35% profit guidance, but evasive on order-conversion specifics, the INR54 crore pipeline stage split, Udaan revenue, and segment data. Management often repeated the same figures and said further detail would come later.
key_quotes: We are confident of achieving a growth of 25% to 30% top line, 30% to 35% in EBITDA and PAT.
Typically in defense industry, H2 is a much stronger period compared to H1.
So, the current margins that we have delivered, we are confident of sustaining it going forward.
Anything more than that is going to be a bonus.

EBITDA/PAT guidance cut to 30-35% from 45-50%, and H1 margin gains were partly FD interest income.
